question: Should default status output show exact cumulative transcript-backed session cost, and if so should it use a bounded or maintained aggregate rather than full transcript scans?
rationale: The user value is clear, but status cost display affects a mature CLI observability surface and the open implementation raises a status responsiveness tradeoff that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Show cost from a bounded aggregate
options.body: Preserve default status responsiveness by using persisted, maintained, cached, or bounded cost data for `/status` and `openclaw status`.

options.title: Accept exact transcript scans
options.body: Allow status to full-scan transcripts for exact cumulative cost, with explicit owner acceptance of the latency and memory tradeoff.

options.title: Defer cost in status
options.body: Keep detailed cost in `/usage cost` and docs until a broader session aggregate design is ready.

recommendation.title: Show cost from a bounded aggregate
recommendation.body: Preserve default status responsiveness by using persisted, maintained, cached, or bounded cost data for `/status` and `openclaw status`.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily on the status rendering and CLI ergonomics surface, where recent history points to vincentkoc.
